newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish PM vows economy to meet EMU goals in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Finnish PM vows economy to meet EMU goals in 1997.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen on Wednesday repeated that the Finnish economy was heading for better times and that Finland would fulfil next year the criteria for the third stage of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"A clear and decisive turn for the better has taken place in the Finnish economy," Lipponen told parliament.
"The gross domestic product is growing at a pace of three to four percent -- the quickest in the European Union," he said.
"Inflation in Finland is the lowest in EU-Europe. Our current account surplus is big and will remain big. Because of this, the nation's external debt is shrinking rapidly," he said.
"Conditions in Finland are very good for continuing growth without accelerating inflation," Lipponen added.

Public sector indebtedness was under control and interest rates -- a key gauge of confidence and credibility both at home and abroad -- had come down clearly since the five-party coalition took office in April 1995, he said.
"Next year, Finland will be among the countries which, having fulfilled the criteria, can join EMU -- if and when EMU is born from the start of 1999," Lipponen said.
He did not elaborate on the EMU criteria and his speech did not mention Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).

Lipponen was speaking in a debate before a confidence vote triggered by the opposition Centre Party, which in an interpellation accused his government of numerous failings including a poor performance in cutting mass unemployment.
Finland is due to hold municipal and European Parliament elections on October 20.
The five parties in Lipponen's left-right-green coalition have a comfortable majority, holding 142 seats out of 200. The Speaker does not vote.
The vote of confidence will be held on September 27 at the start of a plenary session beginning at 1300/1000 GMT, a parliament spokeswoman said.
